fact: Housing Minister Ahmed Dangiwa said over 90 per cent of land in Nigeria remains unregistered and untitled.

The federal government plans to develop and launch a national digital land information system to centralise and digitise land records, and the minister said several state governments are establishing geographic information systems in their land administration.

The Minister of Housing and Urban Development inspected the Centralised Land Repository and Management System, built by Barnksforte Technologies, a platform developed ahead of its official launch with no go-live date stated.
system: Centralised Land Repository and Management System (CLRMS)

fact: The Housing and Urban Development Minister said on 16 July 2026 that the ministry is advancing digital cadastral mapping, electronic land records and a Centralised Lands Repository Management System, alongside the Nigerian Land Titling, Registration and Documentation Programme.

Nugi Technologies says Cross River State's 360Lands digital land registry is in service and has processed 330 title and consent applications, with field officers capturing ownership data into a searchable property database.
Nugi Technologies says applications for a Certificate of Occupancy on 360Lands can be submitted online or at designated offices.

Nigeria Housing Market reports that a federal delegation praised the Edo State Geographic Information Service (EdoGIS) for aligning with national efforts to digitise land records, under a World Bank-backed federal land titling and documentation programme.
BusinessDay reports Lagos State's e-GIS portal went live in January 2024 holding digitised land titles and records for the state.
BusinessDay says anyone can search, verify and apply for land titles including Governor's Consent through the Lagos e-GIS portal online.
